correctness.rationale: In residual coordinates each exact all-but-one update projects onto the normal to the retained columns. The two nonorthogonal normals can be chosen with dot product rho; all others are mutually orthogonal and orthogonal to the pair. For a fixed sample string the squared norm is its first-direction squared projection times the squared overlaps of successive normals. Averaging gives a pair block h_1 P_1+h_2 P_2 and the separate eigenvalues p_j^K for j>=3. Fix positive pair mass t. The bisector tests the pair block at (1+rho)(h_1+h_2)/2, attaining its top eigenvalue at balance. In the path expansion for h_1+h_2 each selected bond set forces the selected field factors to be precisely its odd-degree vertices. Hence only even powers of the imbalance appear, all with nonnegative coefficients; one selected bond gives a positive quadratic term when K>=2. This proves strictness at all imbalances, including boundary probabilities. For K=1 the pair trace is fixed and the determinant (1-rho^2)p_1 p_2 is uniquely maximized at balance. At t=0 the block is zero. The two lower bounds on the K-th root, C_K t/2 and (1-t)/(n-2), intersect at a unique interior pair mass; both are active and enforce exact balance in each group at an optimum, including n=3 with only one orthogonal direction. This gives the claimed sampler and sharp value. For the one-step law its orthogonal block dominates at every K and has retention r_1^K; the K-th root of the ratio tends to r_1/r_infinity>1. The proof concerns exact fixed iid sampling and terminal expected objective, not adaptive or pathwise extrema. The shipped verification was inspected, not rerun; its reported 864 finite checks support the projection and recurrence, not the minimax proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An expected iterate does not determine the expected squared norm. A weak-coupling asymptotic statement cannot specialize to the exact laws and strict uniqueness at every allowed correlation. The general one-step formula specializes exactly at K=1 but not at K>=2.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The all-horizon result needs the imbalance comparison of a finite path partition function and balancing of two active terminal spectral blocks; neither follows by iterating the one-step minimax formula or using exact dynamics at one prescribed law. The same-day overlap is meaningful but does not imply the sharp formula or its global domain.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim is the exact unique optimizer and sharp value for each K>=2 and every 0<rho<1 in the specified one-pair family, with quantified loss from the one-step law. The K=1 case is already covered, and the broad horizon-dependence phenomenon also occurs in a same-day result; neither is credited as independently new here.
residual_risks: A finite-horizon exact design result under different projection or sensor-sampling terminology might cover the optimizer and was not established in this bounded search.
The same-day star result establishes conceptual overlap; no claim of priority for horizon dependence as a general phenomenon is warranted.

value.rationale: One nonorthogonal pair is the smallest residual geometry where mixing two types of errors can change the optimal law with the horizon. The exact optimum, strictness, and exponentially growing worst-case penalty of a one-step-optimal fixed law quantify a real distinction between tuning a one-step contraction and tuning terminal performance. The evidence does not generalize to dense Gram matrices, nonstationary or adaptive sampling, or time-based costs.
